title: Hogwarts Pest Banisher
premise: A touch-first arcade survival game where the player uses wand-like drag gestures to banish cursed magical pests before they overwhelm protected Hogwarts spaces.
interaction_model: Single-screen drag-and-release hazard removal on mouse and touch input.
objective: Keep ward integrity from collapsing by quickly dragging magical pests far enough away to banish them and earn score.
progression: Core source game is endless survival with a rising spawn rate; the remix safely supports a conceptual five-level Hogwarts journey through escalating world presentation and pressure framing.
theme: Harry Potter-inspired wizard school cleanup under magical infestation pressure.
mood: Playful magical urgency with escalating danger and recognizable castle-world wonder.
likely_audience: players who enjoy recognizable fantasy school themes
players who like reactive drag-based action
confidence_notes: High confidence in the drag-to-remove arcade loop.
High confidence that health loss begins when bugs linger too long.
High confidence that explicit multi-level progression is not yet implemented in source.
Moderate confidence that the large foot illustration should be reinterpreted rather than mechanically altered.
source_game_summary: The source game is a one-screen arcade survival title where bugs spawn on a foot-themed playfield and the player drags them away before they damage a health meter. Score increases on each successful clear, health restores on clears, and the game ends at zero health.
remix_prompt_interpretation: Harry Potter should be expressed as a safe thematic conversion: wizarding pests, banishing magic, Hogwarts environments, magical wards, and visual progression through iconic school spaces, without changing the protected drag-removal mechanics.
transform_elements: optional audio mapping using approved remote catalog sources
recreation_prompt: Create a Harry Potter-inspired mobile-first arcade survival game set across magical Hogwarts spaces. The player should see a single-screen playfield and use touch or mouse drag gestures like wand-guided banishing flicks to remove cursed magical pests that appear on protected wizarding surfaces. Each pest must be pressed, dragged, and moved far enough from its origin to count as banished. If pests stay too long, a ward integrity meter should drain continuously, and the game ends when it reaches zero. Successful banishes should raise the score and restore some integrity. Keep the loop immediate, readable, and touch-safe, with a start screen, active play state, and game-over screen. Present the world with recognizable wizard-school motifs such as castle corridors, potion rooms, library aisles, owl-post spaces, and moonlit battlements. Use reactive magical particles, wand-like pointer feedback, clear HUD labels, escalating ambience, and a conceptual five-level Hogwarts progression expressed mainly through presentation and pressure rather than mechanic rewrites.
